channel.title: OnlyBills articles
channel.description: Splitting the bill, tipping and money with friends.

item.title: Can you ask a restaurant to split the bill?
item.description: Yes, most UK restaurants will split a bill. How staff feel about it, how to ask so it's easy for them, and when one card and settling up is kinder.

item.title: Nobody carries cash any more. So who pays?
item.description: Cash was 8% of UK payments in 2025, down from 45% in 2015. What that did to splitting the bill, and what replaced the pile of notes on the table.

item.title: The cost of going out in the UK, and how to spend less
item.description: Half of Brits have turned down an invitation because of the cost, 63% in London. What going out costs now, and practical ways to socialise for less.

item.title: Pay your share without downloading an app
item.description: How web links, App Clips and bank payment links let friends join a split and pay you back with no new app or account, and what each one can see about you.

item.title: How to split a bill for a large group (10 to 30 people)
item.description: A calm method for splitting a big group bill: set menus, deposits, drinks, service charge and one card. Worked £ example for 18 people, plus messages to copy.

item.title: How to split service charge and tips fairly
item.description: Share service charge, tips and discounts in proportion to what each person ordered, not equally. The method, a worked example, and the missing penny fix.

item.title: How to split costs on a group holiday
item.description: Kitty, pay as you go, or one person pays and you settle at the end? How to split meals and costs on a group holiday, with examples and the card fees to avoid.

item.title: Is service charge mandatory in the UK?
item.description: A discretionary service charge is optional and you can ask for it to be removed. When a charge is compulsory, what the 2024 tips law changed, and what to say.

item.title: Who pays on a first date in the UK?
item.description: Splitting is the top answer in UK polls, but many still think the man or the inviter should pay. What surveys say, and how to offer to split gracefully.

item.title: How to split a takeaway order fairly
item.description: Who pays the delivery fee, the service fee and the tip on a group takeaway? A fair method, a worked example and what Deliveroo, Uber Eats and Just Eat offer.

item.title: How much should you tip in the UK?
item.description: In UK restaurants, 10% to 12.5% is normal if there's no service charge, and nothing extra if there is. Here's what's normal in pubs, cafés, taxis and more.

item.title: How to split costs on a stag or hen do
item.description: Deposits, covering the bride or groom, the organiser's float, dinners vs activities and dropouts. A fair way to split stag and hen do costs, with £ examples.

item.title: How to split a bill on iPhone
item.description: Four ways to split a bill on iPhone in the UK: Calculator, Math Notes, Live Text and apps, plus why Apple Cash won't help you here and how to get paid back.

item.title: Birthday dinner: who pays, and should the birthday person?
item.description: Who pays at a UK birthday dinner, whether the birthday person should pay, and how to split it so they're covered, with a worked £ example and messages.

item.title: How to split the bill when some people don't drink
item.description: Non-drinkers often pay for everyone's wine on an equal split. Here's a fair way to split food and drinks, a worked £ example, and what to say at the table.

item.title: How to split a bill with Monzo, Revolut and Starling
item.description: Step by step: the split bill features in Monzo, Revolut and Starling, what they can't do, and how friends at other banks pay you back with a link.

item.title: Is splitting the bill equally fair?
item.description: Splitting equally is fair when everyone had about the same. When orders differ by more than £5, it isn't. Here's a simple rule, worked examples and what to say.

item.title: What to do when someone won't pay their share of the bill
item.description: A friend who always "forgets" to pay? Calm steps from a nudge to a direct chat, messages to copy, how to stop it next time and when it's worth letting go.

item.title: OnlyBills vs Splitwise: which should you use?
item.description: Splitwise is built for running balances and now splits receipts too. OnlyBills is built for UK restaurant bills. Here's when to use which, and how to use both.

item.title: Bill splitting etiquette: 12 unwritten rules for the UK
item.description: The unwritten rules of splitting a restaurant bill in the UK, from agreeing the method early to drinks, service charge and paying back the same day.

item.title: Why groups order more when they split the bill
item.description: In a real restaurant experiment, diners spent about 36% more when the bill was split equally. The diner's dilemma in plain English, and what to do.

item.title: How to ask a friend to pay you back
item.description: Ask the same day, give the exact amount and send a way to pay. Copyable text and WhatsApp messages for dinners, trips, tickets and gentle reminders.

item.title: The best apps for splitting a restaurant bill in 2026
item.description: Splitwise, Tricount, Settle Up, Splid, Tab, your bank's split button and OnlyBills compared: features, UK prices and who each one suits best.

item.title: Splitting the bill equally could be costing you hundreds
item.description: UK diners who lose out on an equal split estimate about £8.73 a meal. Here's what that adds up to over a year, with a worked example and a quick fix.
